artists.biography: Monster Magnet is an American stoner rock band. Hailing from Red Bank, New Jersey, the group was founded by Dave Wyndorf (vocals and guitar), John McBain (guitar) and Tim Cronin (vocals and drums). The band first went by the names "Dog of Mystery", "Airport 75", "Triple Bad Acid" and "King Fuzz" before finally settling on "Monster Magnet", taken from the name of a 1960s toy made by Wham-O, which Wyndorf liked when he was a child.

perplexity.description:
God Says No" is the fifth studio album by American rock band Monster Magnet, originally released in 2000 in Europe and in 2001 in the United States. The album is rooted in hard rock and stoner rock, characterized by heavy guitar riffs, psychedelic textures, and Dave Wyndorf's signature vocal delivery. Musically, it continues the band's tradition of blending fuzz-laden grooves with spacey, retro-inspired atmospheres, while also incorporating elements of blues rock and garage rock. The production is raw and energetic, reflecting a more stripped-down approach compared to their previous major-label releases.

Within Monster Magnet's discography, "God Says No" marks a transitional period, following the commercial success of "Powertrip" (1998). While it retains the band's core sound, it received a cooler reception from both critics and audiences, failing to match the impact of its predecessor. The album was released under A&M Records, with later reissues handled by labels such as Spinefarm Records and Universal Music Group. Commercially, "God Says No" underperformed, and reviews were mixed, with some praising its authenticity and others criticizing its lack of innovation. Despite this, it remains a notable entry for fans of the band's heavier, more psychedelic-oriented work.
